cells.cite: K3.14, K1.6, K2.3, K4.1, K4.3, §28.3 (Owned-local discharge requirement; Diagnostics), §28.9 (trivial-dispose free), §29.2, §35.5, §22.4, §30.5 (Pattern B result), App. C.3
cells.note: Every R1 sub-shape (plain/adopted owned local, `out owned` recipient, owning iteration variable, owning-match arm binding, Pattern B `await` result, `owned` parameter of a synchronous body or lambda) is disposed once at its normal-exit scope end (parameters: method end) unless moved-from or explicitly disposed; a trivial-dispose value is freed at the same point with no lint (K1.6). A later use is statically bounded for locals, returns and captures (K2.3); the only surviving aliases are field- or collection-held borrows admitted under the K4.3-recorded clauses, backstopped by K4.1. Hunted: a plain-parameter callee that stored the borrow (recorded residual, flag-backstopped), an owning iteration variable on the fall-through edge (§29.2: checked as the body's end). No escape. cells.rule: §28.10: "`using var` declares a local that is disposed when the enclosing block ends" | §28.10: "The scoped await-bind ([§30.5](#sec-the-scoped-await-bind)) establishes a compiler-introduced, unnameable slot of exactly this section's kind on the same establishment-ordered cleanup stack" | §29.2: "Both `__source` and `__enumerator` are disposed on every exit path" | §28.10: "the `using var` does **not** assume a disposal obligation (derives: [K2](#sec-kernel-k2) — no obligation can be assumed from a borrow): at scope end, no `Dispose()` is called, because the value is not owned by this scope" | §28.10: "an explicit `Dispose()` of the source is permitted, and a read through the pinned binding afterwards raises `DisposedAccessException` in checked disposal mode" | §28.12: "`await using` is the async counterpart of `using var`" | A12: "Pattern A chaining's disposal-timing dispensation for a `using var` source (deferral to the outer task's teardown)"

cells.note: A `using var` (named, anonymous, `await using`, the scoped await-bind's hidden slot, an owning `__source`/`__enumerator`) is disposed once at its block end in reverse establishment order; `await using` awaits the run-time object's `DisposeAsync` there (§28.12). The borrow-pin form owns nothing; a site-announced kill of its source is admitted and the later read through the pin is flag-backstopped. A15's self-returned enumerator is disposed without reclaim, so `__source`/`__enumerator` naming one object stay exactly-once. A12 moves the moment of a `return await` source's disposal to the outer task's teardown (C10's cell; exactly-once transitively). No escape found.

cells.rule: K8.1: "Unbound owned temporaries are disposed at their full expression's end, after their uses; on the exception edge, during unwinding in reverse production order." | K8.3: "A `case` scrutinee's boundary is the whole construct" | K8.5: "a binding whose initializer is an owned production is a **named unbound owned temporary** whose boundary is the atom — disposed at the atom's completion if undischarged" | §28.3: "for such an operand the disposal is deferred to the end of the full expression rather than performed at the await, so the borrowed result outlives its uses" | K8.4: "a borrow or frame that would escape it is **rejected, never lifetime-extended**" | §28.3: "the stored borrow dangles from the boundary on, and the temporary is not lifetime-extended" | §28.3: "For *field-held* and *collection-held* borrows ([§28.11](#sec-borrowing-collections)'s store rule), liveness holds up to the caller-side lifetime obligations of the bullets above, backstopped by checked disposal mode."
cells.cite: K8.1–K8.5, K3.15, §28.3 (Unbound owned temporaries; A callee that stores a plain argument), §17.13, §17.15, §30.3, §30.5, §35.5 (owning match over a temporary), App. C.3
cells.note: A full-expression temporary is disposed once at its K8 boundary after its uses: statement end, per-evaluation for conditions and guards (K8.2), the whole `case` for a scrutinee (K8.3), the atom for a binding-atom binding (K8.5), the full expression for a Pattern A `await`/`.Result` operand; a trivial-dispose temporary is freed there. Every comparable escape is rejected (K8.4); a callee that stores a plain argument holds it under the recorded borrowed-field residual, backstopped by K4.1. Temporaries that transferred (owned argument, binding, owned slot, return) leave this rule; the return case is R3/C2's open route.

cells.rule: K9: "it is discharged by the destructor cascade (owned fields, reverse declaration order) or by drop-on-overwrite, never by any scope's end, and no scope-end machinery ever touches it" | §28.4: "Disposes all owned-bearing fields in reverse declaration order." | §28.6: "The call is an **early release point**, not a discharge of the slot's obligation: the slot keeps its reference and its [K9](#sec-kernel-k9) obligation, and the containing object's teardown still runs the cascade over it" | §28.6: "so the reader is [K4.1](#sec-kernel-k4)'s backstop: a member access through it raises `DisposedAccessException` in checked disposal mode and is undefined unchecked" | §28.9: "the containing object's teardown for `owned` fields"
cells.cite: K9, K9.1, K4.1, K4.3, §28.4, §28.5, §28.6 (*Who may call Dispose()*), §28.9, §22.10 (capture fields), §28.13 (handles are ordinary owned instances), App. C.3
cells.note: The field's obligation is the object's: discharged once by the owning object's generated `Dispose()` (destructor body, then owned-bearing fields in reverse declaration order, then the base chain), whenever that object is itself released; a trivial-dispose field is freed there. An explicit early `Dispose()` by the declaring type leaves the cascade's second call a no-op; a later read of the field is K4.1-backstopped (§28.6 states it). Receiver-sourced borrows are bounded by the receiver; field-held borrows of the field are the recorded K4.3 clause. Owned primary-constructor capture fields and `Shared<T>` handle fields are ordinary owned fields here. No escape.

A borrowing-match binding that outlives a field's destruction reads the §9.4 disposed state, flag-tested in checked mode. Wholly moved-from locals are skipped (K1 state 3). No escape found.

cells.rule: §30.5: "the task **owns the result** and its destructor disposes it directly" | §30.5: "the outer destructor disposes the chained source task, never the borrowed result directly" | §30.5: "the outer task's teardown disposes **nothing** on that link" | §30.5: "disposing the task disposes the result if one was produced" | §31.1: "disposes the exception after the matching catch arm completes (or after the exception terminates the program if uncaught)" | §30.9: "The exception is disposed **exactly once, by the task that owns it, when the task is disposed**" | §31.4: "The cached `TypeInitializationException` and its `InnerException` are runtime-owned for the life of the process" | §30.11: "For either kind, a **never-awaited** task is disposed exactly once, by the source at source disposal."
cells.note: once-backstopped: a Pattern A result is disposed by its task's teardown (kind 1 directly, kind 2 through the chained task, kind 3 nothing); a Pattern B result transfers at the await or is disposed with the unconsumed task (a continuation if not yet produced); an in-flight exception is disposed after the matching arm, or at termination; a fault exception with its task; a completion source's task by the source. Kind-3 borrows ride the K4.3-recorded residual with the K4.1 backstop. exempt: the cached `TypeInitializationException` (runtime-owned for the process) and a task held by an admitted non-`owned` static (§22.13 exemption) are reclaimed at process exit, not disposed. No escape found.

cells.rule: §30.1: "any `owned` parameter never moved out is disposed by the frame when the task reaches its terminal state — on every completion path (success, fault, and cancellation)" | §29.8: "An iterator method may take `owned` parameters. The state machine takes ownership at construction time. When the iterator is disposed, the state machine disposes any `owned` parameter that has not been moved out of by the body." | §29.8 (Echo): "// No using var: source is disposed by the iterator state machine when the" | §29.3: "An iterator method's return type is `IEnumerable<T>` (re-iterable: each call to `GetEnumerator()` runs the body again from the start)" | K6.1: "**completion or disposal** for an iterator frame" | K6.3: "produces a fresh **owned** frame at every call site"
cells.note: Async frames (task-shaped) are decided: undischarged `owned` parameters and frame locals are disposed once at the task's terminal state, after the body's cleanups. Iterator frames are not: §29.8 says the state machine takes the parameter at construction (the call that mints the enumerable) and disposes it 'when the iterator is disposed', while its own Echo comment and §29.11 name the enumerator. For a re-iterable return type the normal release point of the parameter is therefore either the enumerable's disposal (reading A) or the first enumerator's (reading B). Under B a never-enumerated enumerable has no stated discharge for its parameter, and a second enumeration re-reads a disposed one (the pilot's R8×C11 escape). Same root cause as the pilot cell; filed under it.

The field is not disposed at program exit and must not hold resources that require explicit cleanup." | §22.13: "Overwriting an admitted mutable static never disposes the displaced referent" | §22.13: "No other Bezel code runs concurrently during the shutdown sequence"
cells.cite: §22.12 (forms (i)–(iv), notes (g)–(h)), §22.13 (Disposal of static owned fields; exemption; abnormal termination), §33.3, §31.4, K2 (always-live source), K4.1
cells.note: once-backstopped: `static owned readonly` fields and static owning-inline-array fields (forms (iv) and (h)) are disposed once by the exit pass, reverse initialization order, slots in reverse slot order, late initializations drained; a destructor in the pass that touches an already-disposed static meets the K4.1 flag. exempt: admitted non-`owned` statics and the referents an admitted mutable static or a form-(iv) whole-field store displaced are reclaimed at process exit, not disposed (§22.13's recorded exemption; the declaration-site warnings name it). Abnormal termination is recorded. Environment.Exit's live frames are the separate route cell.

cells.rule: K1.6: "Values of runtime-managed type (`string`, `Type`, boxed value types, function values) and of ordinary value type carry no classification and no obligation" | §28.9: "a closure cannot extend the lifetime of an owned class instance, so reclaiming the closure never leaves a destructor un-run" | §28.8: "the boxed wrapper is a runtime-managed value ([§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types); [K1.6](#sec-kernel-k1)), not an owned `new`-result"
cells.note: No obligation exists to release. Hunted the leak into an obligation-bearing path: a closure over an owned local captures a borrow bounded by the local's scope and may not consume it; a box's payload is fixed and an owning choice cannot be boxed; `Type` is never compiler-freed. No runtime-managed holder keeps an owned referent alive past its owner.

cells.rule: §21.5: "On the way to its target, the jump exits every intervening scope — inner loop bodies, `do … end` blocks, `try` bodies — and each performs its ordinary exit obligations" | §28.10: "on *every* exit edge (normal, `return`, `break`/`continue`, exception, and an iterator's early disposal, [§29.7](#sec-disposal-of-partially-consumed-iterators)), pending cleanups run in reverse order of establishment" | K3.2 row: "none here — the caller's" | §28.4: "The exception propagates from the **disposal point** — the explicit `Dispose()` call, the `using var`/auto-drop scope-end site" | §22.3: "ownership reaches the caller only on normal return, so the value has exactly one owner at every instant"
cells.cite: §21.5, §21.7, §28.3 (Owned-local discharge; Exception-path discharge), §28.4, §28.10, §31.2, K3.2, K3.14, K3.15, §22.3 (the `out owned` contrast), App. C.3
cells.note: once: every structured exit (`return`, labeled or unlabeled `break`/`continue`, a catch-arm exit, `yield break`) runs the scope's cleanups on one establishment-ordered stack, and each owned local or `owned` parameter not moved-from is auto-dropped there once. undetermined: `return x` (or `return <owned expr>`) under an `owned` return moves the value to 'the caller' (K3.2) before the return edge's cleanups run; when one of them raises (a throwing `finally`, a `using var` or auto-drop disposer), the call never returns, the binding is moved-from, and no rule names the holder of the in-transit value. §22.3 decides exactly this shape for `out owned` (copy-out on normal return only); the return slot has no counterpart.

cells.rule: §28.10: "Disposal happens on every exit path: normal completion, `break`, `return`, or exception." | §29.2: "`break` exits the surrounding `do ... end`, triggering disposal of both." | §28.12: "Asynchronous cleanup runs only where the program wrote `await using` (whose implicit `finally` awaits `DisposeAsync` on both the normal and exception edges of an async body" | §30.5: "On an early `return`, the slot's disposal runs during that return's scope exit, after `x`'s last use." | A5: "`using var` is a scope pin: non-reassignable, never movable out"
cells.note: A `using var`, `await using var`, scoped await-bind slot or owning `__source`/`__enumerator` is disposed once on the early exit's scope exit, in reverse establishment order with `finally` blocks; `await using` awaits on the edge in an async body; `yield break` exits the iterator body the same way. A5 forbids moving out, so no structured exit can leave a pinned value with two holders. A12's `return await` over a `using var` defers its disposal to the outer task (C10). The raising-cleanup-on-a-return edge leaks the returned value, not the pinned one (R1/C2).

cells.rule: K3.15: "Unbound temporaries join the same stack at their production." | K8.3: "the temporary survives arm selection, guard evaluation, and the selected arm's completion — in statement position exactly as in expression position" | §28.3: "A temporary that had already transferred — into an `owned` parameter, a binding, an owned slot, or a return — is not disposed by this pass (its new owner's rules govern)" | K3.2 row: "none here — the caller's"
cells.note: once: the only temporaries that can be live at a structured exit are a statement-`case` scrutinee (K8.3, an arm that `return`s or `break`s) and an owning match's consumed value; both sit on the cleanup stack from production (K3.15) and §28.10 runs that stack on every exit edge. undetermined: a fresh owned `return` operand transfers 'into a return' and leaves this rule, then a raising cleanup on the return edge leaves it with no holder (same root cause as R1/C2).

cells.rule: K9.2: "every control-flow path from a `move` of a field or slot to the enclosing method's exit — normal, `throw`, `yield break`, and every exception edge raised by an intervening throwable expression — must reassign the slot" | §28.8.1: "The exit paths considered include normal return, fall-through (for `()`-returning methods), `throw`, `yield break` (in iterator methods), and any other transfer of control that leaves the method body." | §28.8.1: "In particular there is no terminal-move dispensation" | §28.8.1: "The rule reads a field of **any** object `x` — `this`, a parameter, or a local holder the method itself disposes" | K9: "never by any scope's end, and no scope-end machinery ever touches it"
cells.cite: K9, K9.2, K9.3, §28.8.1 (The field-restoration rule; Loops; Detaching), §28.6; #5725 (non-`this` receivers, implementation), #5667
cells.note: A structured exit never discharges a field (K9); it only crosses a K9.2 restoration window, and every exit that leaves the method body must have restored a moved field — a `break`/`continue` inside the body is not a method exit and stays inside the window. A terminal `return move _f;` is rejected. The field is therefore discharged once, by its owner's cascade. #5725 tracks the non-`this` receiver implementation. The in-window re-entrant observation of the hole is the route cell R4/C3·reentrant.

cells.rule: §28.11: "The compiler tracks moved-from state per slot when the index is a compile-time constant or a local read." | §28.11: "after `move coll[i]` with a non-constant `i`, the *entire collection* is treated as having one or more slots in moved-from state" | §28.11: "`coll[j] := value` for any `j` (treated as restoration of one slot if `j` matches the moved index, or as unrelated reassignment otherwise)" | K9.2: "the object must never escape the method with a hole a destructor could observe" | §28.11: "partial iteration drains only the elements yielded, and the rest remain"
cells.cite: K9.2, §28.11 (`move` on a collection slot; Owning collections), §28.8.1, §29.1, §29.2, stdlib §4.5
cells.note: once: early exits from a `Drain()` loop leave the undrained elements owned by the collection and dispose the enumerator; a constant- or local-indexed `move coll[i]` must be restored on every exit. ambiguous: with a non-constant index the whole collection is tracked as holed, and §28.11 lists `coll[j] := value` 'for any `j`' among the admissible restorations. Reading A: any such store discharges the obligation, so a run with j ≠ i leaves slot i a hole at the exit, exactly what K9.2 forbids (at an `[N owned]T` slot §15.3 calls auto-dispose of a moved-from slot 'not defined'). Reading B: the store restores only a provably-matching index, so 'for any `j`' admits nothing beyond `Clear()`/`Dispose()`. A second wrinkle: the store may hit a live slot, which makes it throwable (§28.8.1), and its own edge is unrestored.

cells.rule: §15.3: "any slot moved-from via `move arr[i]` must be reassigned before any exit edge, because auto-dispose on a moved-from slot is not defined" | §15.3: "**Return**: returning a move-only value transfers it to the caller. The callee's local is moved-from after the return." | §35.5: "In an owning match, an `owned`-payload binding (`var r` above) is an **owned local of the arm body's scope**" | §28.11: "`arr[j] := value` for any `j` (for nullable forms, `arr[j] := null` is also a valid restoration that marks slots empty)"
cells.note: once: move-only locals, an owning match's consumed value (a `move` result or temporary on the cleanup stack) and owning-match bindings are disposed once on every structured exit; a moved slot must be restored before the method exit. Two open sub-shapes: (1) a move-only value returned through a raising cleanup on the return edge has no holder (L1-RC1, same as R1/C2); (2) a non-constant-index `move arr[i]` on an owning inline array is restorable by 'arr[j] := value for any j' (L1-RC2), which at `[N owned]T` leaves a slot whose auto-dispose §15.3 calls 'not defined'.

cells.rule: §31.1: "disposes the exception after the matching catch arm completes (or after the exception terminates the program if uncaught)" | §31.1: "since it transfers the in-flight exception back to the runtime rather than capturing it" | §31.2: "on the exception edge such a jump would silently discard the in-flight exception" | §29.6: "the exception itself disposed once the arm completes" | §30.5: "A `return` in an `async` body — an `async` method's or an `async` lambda's — whose return type is `Task<T>` for class or interface T, whose operand is a **borrow** and not a `return await`"
cells.note: An in-flight exception reaches a structured exit only from a catch arm (`return`, `break`, `continue`, a fresh `throw`): its handling ends with the arm and the runtime disposes it once; a bare re-raise hands it back undisposed. Jumps out of a `finally` that could abandon it are rejected, and `yield` in an arm is rejected. A task result reached by an early `return` in an async body is one of §30.5's three kinds. Editorial note: 'completes' is not defined for an arm left by a jump or a throw; the only sensible reading (every arm exit ends handling) is the one taken here, and §29.6's 'would end the arm without completing it' leans on a narrower sense.

cells.rule: §29.3: "`yield break;` terminates iteration. Falling off the end of the method has the same effect as `yield break`." | §30.1: "any `owned` parameter never moved out is disposed by the frame when the task reaches its terminal state — on every completion path (success, fault, and cancellation), after the body's `using var` cleanups and `finally` clauses" | K3.2 row: "the task's result, [§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal)'s Pattern B transfer and Pattern A kind 1 (disposed by the awaiter or by the task's teardown, as §30.5 states)" | §30.5: "A task that has been awaited and faulted, or awaited and cancelled, has no owned result to dispose; disposal is a no-op for the result."
cells.note: once: `yield break` and `return` exit the frame body through its cleanups; frame-held `owned` parameters are disposed by the frame at teardown/terminal state. undetermined: in an `async` body, `return <owned>` under `OwningTask<T>` (or Pattern A kind 1) moves the value toward the task's result slot, then a raising cleanup on the return edge faults the task; §30.5 says a faulted task 'has no owned result to dispose', and no rule says whether the returned value was recorded (task teardown disposes it) or not (leak). Async twin of L1-RC1.

cells.rule: K9: "never by any scope's end, and no scope-end machinery ever touches it" | K9.4: "static owned fields admit no `move`" | §22.12: "slot stores, `move arr[j]`, and per-slot restoration follow [§15.1.1](#sec-owning-inline-arrays) unchanged" | K9.2: "every control-flow path from a `move` of a field or slot to the enclosing method's exit"
cells.note: Re-verified pilot cell; verdict changed from n/a to once. K9 and K9.4 hold for `static owned readonly` fields (no scope end touches them; no `move`). But §22.12 form (iv) admits `move arr[j]` on a mutable static owning inline array with per-slot restoration, so a static slot can sit in a K9.2 window that a `return`/`break`/`yield break` crosses; K9.2 requires restoration before the method exit, so the slot is still discharged once by the exit pass. Tension recorded, not a conflict: K9.4's stated ground ('static state is observable across method boundaries, so no per-method window can cover it') applies equally to form-(iv) slots, which the letter of K9.4 does not reach; the in-window observation is the route cell R4/C3·reentrant.

cells.rule: K1.6: "Values of runtime-managed type (`string`, `Type`, boxed value types, function values) and of ordinary value type carry no classification and no obligation" | §28.9: "a `using var` local of function type is nonetheless permitted (disposal at scope end is a no-op)"
cells.note: Nothing to discharge on any exit; a `using var` over a runtime-managed value is a no-op disposal. A closure value leaving a scope through `return` is rejected when it captures a borrow of a scope-bound source (§28.3 closure bullet), so no exit path carries an owned referent out inside a runtime-managed value.

cells.rule: K3.15: "**Edge parity.** The exception edge performs the same implicit disposal as the normal edge, on the single establishment-ordered cleanup stack; the only difference is the lint." | §28.3: "Owned locals and owned parameters that are live when an exception propagates out of their enclosing block are disposed implicitly during stack unwinding" | §28.8.1: "the caller's binding is moved-from on the exception edge exactly as on the normal one, and the value is discharged on the callee's side" | §22.3: "For `out owned`, the callee-local slot is an owned slot: a value assigned to it before a later `throw` is discharged by the callee's ordinary exception-path discharge" | §28.7: "A throwing RHS leaves the field/local untouched and still-owned"
cells.note: Re-verified the pilot cell: unchanged. Added hunts: an `out owned` value assigned before a callee throw (callee-side discharge; the caller's recipient is unassigned and owes nothing, §22.3/§22.4); an owning iteration variable and an owning-match arm binding on an arm's throw (exception-path discharge); `x.Dispose()` whose destructor throws (remaining steps run and the flag is set, §28.4, so the unwind's second call is §28.2's no-op: exactly-once of the destructor holds by idempotence).

cells.rule: §28.10: "Disposal happens on every exit path: normal completion, `break`, `return`, or exception." | §28.12: "when `DisposeAsync` completes **by throwing**, logical disposal is over — the runtime performs physical reclamation, then the exception propagates from the await" | §30.5: "If `E`'s production or the await faults, the already-produced task is disposed during unwinding by the same establishment-ordered pass that covers a hand-written `using var`" | §28.4: "a throwing disposer does not skip the remaining values: every remaining disposal still runs" | §31.2: "the superseded exception is **disposed by the runtime exactly once**"
cells.note: Every pinned owned slot is disposed once on the exception edge in establishment order with `finally` blocks; `await using` awaits `DisposeAsync` on that edge too, and a throwing `DisposeAsync` still reclaims. A throwing disposer in the unwind does not skip the rest; each later throw supersedes, the superseded exception recorded then disposed. Disposing `__enumerator` on a body exception runs the iterator's pending cleanup (§29.7), whose throws join the same discipline. No escape.

cells.rule: §28.3: "every already-produced, not-yet-consumed unbound owned temporary is disposed during unwinding by the same implicit `try`/`finally` mechanism as named locals" | §28.3: "a temporary whose producing subexpression never ran was never produced" | §28.7: "a throwing disposer during overwrite propagates after the store is abandoned, leaving the new value an unbound owned temporary disposed by [§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries)'s unbound-temporary rule — on this exception edge, during the unwind" | §35.5: "An exception out of an arm disposes the not-yet-consumed remainder during unwinding ([K3.15](#sec-kernel-k3))." | §30.9: "a task disposed while its own fault exception is in flight defers that disposal until the exception's handling completes"
cells.note: Each produced, untransferred temporary is disposed once during the unwind in reverse production order, under §28.4's multi-value discipline; one already transferred into an `owned` parameter is the callee's (§28.8.1). The abandoned-store RHS and an owning match's remainder are temporaries of this pass. A Pattern A `await` operand temporary unwound by its own fault defers disposing the fault until handling completes. No escape.

cells.rule: K9.2: "and every exception edge raised by an intervening throwable expression — must reassign the slot" | §28.8.1: "A restoration placed in a `finally` satisfies the rule as well, when every throwable expression between the move and the store lies in that `try`'s protected block" | K9.5: "drop-on-overwrite (K3.11) is RHS-first, so a throwing RHS leaves the slot untouched and still-owned" | §28.4: "the remaining owned-field disposals (reverse declaration order) and the base-class chain complete, and physical reclamation still occurs"
cells.cite: K9.2, K9.5, §28.4, §28.7, §28.8.1 (Exception paths are not exempt), §22.9 (C4's), §31.2; #5667 (finally restoration, implementation), #5725
cells.note: A field is never discharged by an unwind; K9.2 requires every exception edge out of a move window to have restored the slot (directly before the throwable, or in a `finally` covering it), so the object's cascade later disposes it once. A throwing RHS leaves the field still owned. A throwing destructor still completes the remaining field disposals. Base cell decided; the in-window re-entrant access that the `finally` form (and an `await`, or a constructor body under `new`) admits is the route cell R4/C3·reentrant.

cells.rule: §28.11: "The same exception-safety rules apply: any throwable expression between the move and the reassignment must be an exit path on which the slot has been restored." | §28.8.1: "If the call then raises — from the callee's body, or from a constructor's field initializers or body ([§22.9](#sec-owned-fields-and-exception-safety)) — the caller's binding is moved-from on the exception edge exactly as on the normal one" | §28.4: "an owning collection's element cascade" | §29.2: "On *exception* edges — whether from an explicit `throw` or from a method call that propagates an exception out of the body — the iteration variable is auto-disposed"
cells.note: A slot's element is disposed once: an ingress member that raises after entry owns its `owned` argument (callee-side discharge), the indexer-set's throwing displaced disposer abandons the store and unwinds the new value, a moved slot is restored on every exception edge, and an unwound owning collection cascades under the multi-value discipline. A Drain loop's iteration variable is unwound; the enumerator's disposal handles the rest. Lead (stdlib, not a cell): the `OwningDictionary.Add` sketch (stdlib §4.9) calls `_comparer.Equals(...)` between `move chain.Next` and its restoration, which K9.2 rejects; a throwing comparer there would also unwind the partly rebuilt chain, destroying entries.

cells.rule: §15.3: "**Exception-path discharge**: on exception edges, the slots are auto-disposed by the implicit `try`/`finally` rule" | §35.5: "An exception out of an arm disposes the not-yet-consumed remainder during unwinding ([K3.15](#sec-kernel-k3))." | §35.5: "If `Validate(r)` throws, `r` — an owned local of the arm-body scope — is disposed by the exception-path discharge" | §35.5: "in expression position `MatchFailureException` is raised ([§19.6](#sec-exhaustiveness)) and the payloads are disposed during unwinding by the standard exception-path machinery" | §28.7: "the remaining live slots are still disposed, and a later throw supersedes an earlier one"
cells.note: Lead hunted: an exception out of an owning-match arm after a partial transfer. The transferred binding is an owned local of the arm (exception-path discharge); the remainder stays with the consumed value, a `move` result or temporary on the cleanup stack, disposed during the unwind; a throwing guard transfers nothing. Move-only locals and parameters unwind slot by slot under §28.4. No escape; #5541/#5642/#5652 are implementation of the disposed states.

cells.rule: §31.2: "the superseded exception is **disposed by the runtime exactly once**, as if its handling had completed — unless it is one of the two [§31.1](#sec-exception-ownership) dispose-after-arm exemptions" | §31.2: "supersession ends the instance's handling, never its life" | §30.9: "a task disposed while its own fault exception is in flight defers that disposal until the exception's handling completes" | §31.2: "and **before** the superseded exception is disposed (or, for the two owner-owned instances above, before it is dropped from the in-flight slot)" | §28.4: "a pass entered **on an exception edge** — the exception-path discharge, and [§22.9](#sec-owned-fields-and-exception-safety)'s construction unwind — carries that exception's own entry as well, ahead of them"
cells.cite: §31.1, §31.2 (supersession; record-before-drop), §31.2.1 (guard), §28.4, §28.12, §30.5 (Pattern B on the fault edge), §30.9, §30.10 (aggregation), §31.4
cells.note: Lead hunted: a task-owned fault F in flight while an `await using` scope unwinds. If the owning task's `using var` is disposed first, F's disposal is deferred until its handling completes; a throwing `DisposeAsync` then supersedes F, which ends F's handling, so the owner's deferred disposal runs once, after F's snapshot is recorded. In the other order F is dropped undisposed and its owner disposes it later. An ordinary superseded exception is recorded, then disposed; a consumed Pattern B operand's deferred disposal is the await's terminal act; `WhenAll` re-raises keep their input task as owner. No escape.

cells.rule: §30.1: "on every completion path (success, fault, and cancellation), after the body's `using var` cleanups and `finally` clauses" | §28.3: "Undischarged `owned` parameters' implicit disposals are established at entry to the body" | §29.8: "If the body does not move ownership out, the state machine disposes the parameter at iterator disposal — after `using var` cleanups within the body and after `finally` clauses." | §29.7: "Transitions to a **completed** state: the machine's own bookkeeping records exhaustion, so nothing resumes and no suspended body runs again."
cells.note: once: an async frame faults its task and disposes undischarged parameters and frame locals at that terminal state. ambiguous: when an exception escapes a synchronous iterator body out of `MoveNext()`, §28.3 disposes a live `owned` parameter during that unwind (its disposal 'established at entry to the body'), while §29.8 disposes it 'at iterator disposal', i.e. when the consumer later disposes the enumerator. Exactly-once survives either way by idempotence, but the moment differs and is observable from the consumer's handler. Neither §29.7 nor §29.8 states the post-fault state: §29.7's completed state is reached only by disposal, so a `MoveNext()` after a caught fault has no stated meaning (resume, `false`, or fault).

cells.rule: K9: "never by any scope's end, and no scope-end machinery ever touches it" | §33.3: "The [§22.13](#sec-static-initialization-order) shutdown sequence (static `owned` disposal) still runs, and it runs with this exception's handling already complete" | §22.12: "slot stores, `move arr[j]`, and per-slot restoration follow [§15.1.1](#sec-owning-inline-arrays) unchanged"
cells.note: An unwind never touches static storage; an exception escaping `Main` reaches the exit pass with nothing in flight, so the pass disposes each static once. A form-(iv) slot moved inside a static method must be restored on every exception edge (K9.2). Static initialization failure is C4's; a throwing static disposer is C12's.

cells.rule: §28.3: "Value-typed and runtime-managed-typed locals; these have no `Dispose` to call." | K1.6: "Values of runtime-managed type (`string`, `Type`, boxed value types, function values) and of ordinary value type carry no classification and no obligation"
cells.note: The unwind skips runtime-managed locals. Hunted: a closure capturing an exception binding or an owned local and outliving the unwind is rejected by the arm-confinement and closure-escape rules; a `string` copied out of an exception (`ex.Message`) holds no reference to it.

cells.rule: §28.8.1: "If the call then raises — from the callee's body, or from a constructor's field initializers or body ([§22.9](#sec-owned-fields-and-exception-safety)) — the caller's binding is moved-from on the exception edge exactly as on the normal one, and the value is discharged on the callee's side" | §22.9: "An `owned` primary parameter that was *not* captured (referenced only in initializer positions) still holds its value on any construction throw before its consuming initializer ran — a step-1 throw, or a step-2 throw from an earlier initializer — and is discharged as an ordinary `owned` parameter by the exception-path discharge" | §22.9: "the capture **moves** the parameter, so no [§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows) parameter-level discharge ever also claims the value" | §28.3: "Owned locals and owned parameters that are live when an exception propagates out of their enclosing block are disposed implicitly during stack unwinding"
cells.cite: §28.8.1 (A raise from the consuming call), §22.9, §22.10 (owned parameters and capture), §28.3 (Exception-path discharge), K3.3, K3.15, App. C.3
cells.note: An `owned` constructor parameter is the callee's from call entry: on any construction throw it is discharged by the constructor's exception-path discharge while undischarged, or by §22.9's owned-field unwind once stored (K3.1 leaves the parameter moved-from, so the two never both claim it); the caller's binding is moved-from on both edges and is unreadable in a `catch` arm. Hunted: `base(move p)` into a throwing base (base side discharges), a captured vs. uncaptured `owned` primary parameter (capture moves it; an uncaptured one is a plain owned parameter until its initializer runs), a conditional store into a field before a throw (per-path). No escape found.

cells.rule: §28.10: "Disposal happens on every exit path: normal completion, `break`, `return`, or exception." | §28.4: "Three actions still run after a constructor body's last statement, and each can throw into that unwind: the constructor's `ensures` clauses and the construction-exit invariant check ([§22.16](#sec-contract-clauses)), and the scope-end disposals of the body's `using var` locals." | §28.4: "a resource acquired in a constructor body and orphaned by a later throw in that body leaks." | K3.15: "**Edge parity.** The exception edge performs the same implicit disposal as the normal edge, on the single establishment-ordered cleanup stack; the only difference is the lint. Unbound temporaries join the same stack at their production."
cells.cite: §28.10, §28.4 (destructor body never on construction unwind; one raw resource per owning wrapper), §22.9, K3.15
cells.note: A `using var` (and the compiler-introduced slots) in a constructor body or field-initializer helper is disposed on the construction-unwind edge exactly as on any exit edge, in establishment order with `finally`. A `using var` scope-end disposal that throws after an acquisition throws into §22.9's unwind; the only thing the text lets leak is a raw resource held in no owned field (an `IntPtr`), which carries no K1 obligation and is §28.4's recorded one-resource-per-wrapper discipline, not an owned-value leak. No escape found for an owned value.

cells.rule: §28.3: "When the full expression is instead exited by an **exception** — an operand or argument evaluated later throws before the temporary's transfer or consumption point — every already-produced, not-yet-consumed unbound owned temporary is disposed during unwinding" | §28.8.1: "where the raise happens **before** the call is entered — a later argument's evaluation throwing — the already-produced temporary has not transferred and is disposed by the caller's unwinding pass." | K3.15: "**Edge parity.** The exception edge performs the same implicit disposal as the normal edge, on the single establishment-ordered cleanup stack; the only difference is the lint. Unbound temporaries join the same stack at their production." | K8: "A **full expression** is a maximal expression — not a subexpression of any larger expression — at the enumerated positions (initializers, assignment RHSs, expression statements, each *evaluation* of a condition or guard, `for` sources, `return`/`throw`/`yield return` operands, `case` scrutinees)."
cells.note: Temporaries produced in a `new` argument list, a field initializer or a constructor body join the cleanup stack at production and are disposed on the construction-throw edge in reverse production order; one already transferred into an `owned` constructor parameter is the callee's (§28.8.1). Decided for C4. Side note for L1/C1: K8's enumerated full-expression positions do not name a constructor's chaining-position arguments (`base(new Res())`, a primary constructor's inheritance-clause call), so the normal-edge boundary of a temporary passed there to a plain base parameter is not stated; the unwind edge is unaffected (K3.15).

cells.rule: §22.9: "When construction throws, the compiler unwinds the partially-constructed instance in **reverse declaration order** within the derived class" | §22.9: "An exception in the **constructor body** (step 3) triggers disposal of every owned field assigned during initialization (step 2) and the base subobject. Owned fields assigned imperatively in the body are also disposed if assigned successfully before the throwing statement." | §28.4: "**The destructor body runs on disposal, never on construction unwind — hold one raw resource per owning wrapper.**" | §28.8.1: "After the first assignment, `move` is permitted, with the same field-restoration rule applying to constructor exit paths." | §22.9: "a disposer that throws during it **supersedes** that exception under [§28.4](#sec-the-destructor)'s rule"
cells.cite: §22.8 (construction sequence, once-only initializers), §22.9, §22.10 (capture fields), §28.4, §28.8.1 (Constructors and destructors; Exception paths are not exempt), K9.2, K9.3
cells.note: Every owned instance field (declared or primary-constructor capture) whose initialization completed is disposed once on each construction-throw edge, captures first, then the base subobject's full `Dispose()`; a fully-initialized `this(...)`-chaining body throw takes the normal generated `Dispose()`. A `move` of an owned field in a constructor body takes K9.2 on the exception edge too, so the unwind never meets a hole. Hunted: field initializer then body reassignment (drop-on-overwrite, single owner), a throwing `ensures`/invariant after the body (§28.4 says it throws into the unwind), a moved-and-unrestored field on a throw edge (rejected). No escape; see R6/C4 for an owning-choice field, which §22.9's pass does not name.

cells.rule: §28.11: "Disposal of the collection itself — at the end of a `using var` scope, in a destructor's auto-dispose pass, or at static-program-exit for a `static owned` field — disposes every element it still holds, then frees the backing storage" | §22.9: "An exception in the **constructor body** (step 3) triggers disposal of every owned field assigned during initialization (step 2) and the base subobject. Owned fields assigned imperatively in the body are also disposed if assigned successfully before the throwing statement." | K3.15: "**Edge parity.** The exception edge performs the same implicit disposal as the normal edge, on the single establishment-ordered cleanup stack; the only difference is the lint. Unbound temporaries join the same stack at their production."
cells.note: An owning collection held in an owned field is disposed by §22.9's unwind and cascades over its elements; one held in a constructor local or temporary is disposed by the exception-path discharge. Elements produced for a literal or an `Add` whose evaluation is cut short by a throw are unbound temporaries (disposed by the unwind) until they are taken by the collection, after which the collection's cascade owns them. No escape found.

cells.rule: §22.9: "the **owned-field disposals** of [§28.4](#sec-the-destructor)'s generated `Dispose()` — that pass and nothing before it" | §28.4: "Disposes all owned-bearing fields in reverse declaration order. This covers fields marked `owned` (class- or interface-typed; the field's value's `Dispose()` is called) and fields of owning-inline-array type" | §28.4: "Inline-array fields without `owned` slots, value-typed fields, and runtime-managed fields require no disposal." | §35.4: "a move-only value carrying no borrows may be a class field (the class's destructor disposes it)" | §15.3: "a move-only value carrying no borrows may be a field of a class; the class's destructor disposes the field's owned slots."
cells.note: Owning-inline-array field: once (named in §28.4 step 2, so in §22.9's unwind; slots reverse, null-guarded). Owning-choice field: §22.9's unwind is exactly §28.4's owned-field disposals, and §28.4 step 2 enumerates `owned` fields and owning-inline-array fields only, putting every other value-typed field under 'require no disposal', while §15.3/§35.4 say the class's destructor disposes an owning-choice field. By the letter, a constructor that assigns `_s := Slot.Full(new Res())` and then throws leaks the payload (and so does normal teardown, R6/C12).

cells.rule: §31.1: "ownership transfers to the runtime's exception machinery, which disposes the exception after the matching catch arm completes (or after the exception terminates the program if uncaught)" | §22.9: "a disposer that throws during it **supersedes** that exception under [§28.4](#sec-the-destructor)'s rule, and the superseded exception is recorded into the superseding one's `SupersededChain` before the drop" | §22.7: "the original exception never propagates raw out of static initialization; it is observable only as `InnerException`." | §31.4: "**The cached `TypeInitializationException` and its `InnerException` are runtime-owned for the life of the process**"
cells.note: Sub-shapes: (1) the in-flight construction exception is the runtime's, disposed once after its catch arm, or superseded during the unwind and then disposed once after its snapshot is recorded: once. (2) A static initializer's escaping exception becomes the cached `TypeInitializationException`'s `InnerException`, and both are runtime-owned for the process and exempt from dispose-after-arm, which is what makes every later re-raise sound: exempt. (3) Supersession of the cached instance drops it undisposed (§31.2). Hunted: re-raising the cached TIE on every touch after a catch arm completed (exempt by name, so no double dispose). No escape.

cells.rule: §29.8: "An iterator method may take `owned` parameters. The state machine takes ownership at construction time." | §30.1: "An async method's `owned` parameters transfer into the state-machine frame at call time, exactly as an iterator's do" | §31.4: "Allocation failure is not an exception. There is no `OutOfMemoryException`; nothing is catchable; no unwinding runs"
cells.note: A frame is constructed by the minting call and no constructor body is a deferred activation, so there is no construction-unwind edge for frame state. Frame construction runs no user code before the `owned` arguments are frame-held; its only failure is allocation failure, which terminates without unwinding (§22.13's abnormal-termination list). An argument whose evaluation throws before the call is entered is R1/R3's caller-side unwind (§28.8.1), and a frame bound to an owned field of an object under construction is R4's.

cells.rule: §22.13: "A static `owned` field whose initializer threw is not disposed (its value was never produced). A static `owned` field on a type left in a failed state ([§22.7](#sec-constructors)) whose initializer *did* complete successfully before the failing initializer is disposed normally." | §22.13: "the pass drains until no initialized-but-undisposed static `owned` field remains" | §22.13: "A static field of owning-inline-array type whose initializer threw is not disposed (the array's slots were never observable)" | §22.13: "A `static readonly` field of class type or interface type that is not marked `owned` is exempt from the [§28.8](#sec-ownership-transfer) ownership-discharge requirement" | §22.7: "The runtime makes no guarantee about ordering of disposal across types when one of the types is in a failed state."
cells.cite: §22.7 (failed state), §22.12 rule 1, §22.13 (cycle backstop; Disposal of static owned fields; exemption), §31.4, K3.15
cells.note: `static owned` and owning-inline-array statics whose value was produced are disposed once at exit even when their type is left failed; one whose initializer threw holds nothing, and the initializer's own temporaries and locals are discharged by the ordinary unwind before the exception becomes the cached TIE's `InnerException`: once. Admitted non-`owned` statics: exempt. A `static owned readonly` field assigned in the static constructor body (no initializer) before a later throw is read as enrolled through the pass's 'initialized-but-undisposed' wording rather than the 'initializer completed' sentences. Cross-type exit order among failed types is explicitly unspecified (order only; exactly-once holds). Re-entrancy raises the synthesized TIE and never observes a half-initialized static.

cells.rule: K1.6: "Values of runtime-managed type (`string`, `Type`, boxed value types, function values) and of ordinary value type carry no classification and no obligation" | §28.9: "a closure cannot extend the lifetime of an owned class instance, so reclaiming the closure never leaves a destructor un-run."
cells.cite: K1.6, §28.1 clauses 2–3, §28.9, §8.6, §35.8 (owning choices cannot be boxed)
cells.note: Strings, `Type`, boxes and function values in fields, initializers or constructor locals carry no obligation to unwind. Hunted for an exemption leak: a closure built in a constructor over an owned local (a capture is a borrow, §28.9; a plain function-typed primary parameter cannot be captured into a field, §22.10), and a boxed owning choice (not admitted, §35.8). No obligation-bearing value hides behind the exemption on this path.

cells.rule: §28.3: "an **owned-state** LHS requires an owned RHS — a fresh producer, or a named owned binding under the explicit transfer marker (`x := move y;`) — and disposes the displaced value per drop-on-overwrite ([§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields)), subject to the consume-site freeze below" | §28.7: "The right-hand side is evaluated first; then, if the previous value is live (non-null and not moved-from — the per-slot tracking [§28.11](#sec-collection-element-ownership)'s indexer-set rule already defines), it is disposed; then the new value is stored." | §28.7: "a throwing disposer during overwrite propagates after the store is abandoned, leaving the new value an unbound owned temporary disposed by [§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries)'s unbound-temporary rule — on this exception edge, during the unwind." | K5: "drop-on-overwrite of a binding (row K3.11) is frozen although it disposes" | §28.3: "not the flag-backstopped kills (the site-announced kills, [K4.2](#sec-kernel-k4), and a reassignment's drop-on-overwrite of the displaced value, [K3.11](#sec-kernel-k3), each runtime-checked under [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal))"
cells.note: The reassigned binding discharges its displaced value once, after the RHS, null-guarded; a moved-from or polymorphic-null LHS adopts with nothing to dispose. Live local borrows freeze the overwrite (K5.2), and a field- or collection-held borrow of the displaced value survives only under the K4.1 flag the drop sets (§28.3's report-mode note names this kill as runtime-checked). A throwing displaced disposer abandons the store and the RHS becomes an unwound temporary; the old value stays bound but flagged, so the unwind's second Dispose relies on §28.2's idempotent no-op (exactly-once kept). Note: §28.7's scope sentence lists 'plain-`var` owned locals' and not `owned` parameters or an `out owned` callee slot, which reach drop-on-overwrite only through K3.11's 'owned location' (editorial, RC6).

cells.rule: A5: "`using var` is a scope pin: non-reassignable, never movable out" | §28.10: "`using var` is a scope pin (axiom [A5](#sec-axiom-register)): it is implicitly non-reassignable, and reassigning a `using var` variable is a compile error." | §28.3: "establishing a hidden, unnameable `using var` slot"
cells.note: Every R2 holder is non-reassignable: a named or anonymous `using var`/`await using var` by A5, and the compiler-introduced slots have no name to assign. A move-only `using var` keeps its slot pass at scope end and only gains the reassignment lock. Displacement cannot reach the holder.

cells.rule: §28.7: "a throwing disposer during overwrite propagates after the store is abandoned, leaving the new value an unbound owned temporary disposed by [§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries)'s unbound-temporary rule — on this exception edge, during the unwind." | §28.3: "A temporary that is instead bound (to a `var`/`using var`), `move`d, returned, or transferred into an owning location is governed by the corresponding transfer or discharge rule and is **not** disposed under this rule (it would otherwise be disposed twice)."
cells.cite: §28.7 (Ordering and exceptions), §28.3 (Unbound owned temporaries), K8.1, K9.5, §15.3
cells.note: An unbound temporary is not a location and cannot be displaced; the one R3 shape on this path is the RHS of an abandoned store (a throwing displaced disposer), which §28.7 makes an unbound owned temporary disposed once by the unwind; the owning-inline-array per-slot pass abandons its store the same way. A binding-atom binding cannot be reassigned inside its single-expression body. No escape found.

cells.rule: §28.7: "The right-hand side is evaluated first; then, if the previous value is live (non-null and not moved-from — the per-slot tracking [§28.11](#sec-collection-element-ownership)'s indexer-set rule already defines), it is disposed; then the new value is stored." | §28.7: "A moved-from or null location therefore stores without disposal" | §28.8.1: "The rule reads a field of **any** object `x` — `this`, a parameter, or a local holder the method itself disposes" | §9.4: "a read of the vacated field through an alias of its holder, which the moved-from state of [§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression) does not track, reads the same state." | §28.11: "The compiler's per-slot moved-from tracking is what makes this distinguishable from a non-moved-from slot, where the setter does dispose the previous value." | §28.8.1: "Stores into provably moved-from or null locations, and stores into borrow-state or value-typed locations, remain non-throwable" | §28.7: "a borrow of the displaced value is invalidated at the overwrite, caught as `DisposedAccessException` in checked disposal mode and undefined unchecked"
cells.cite: §28.7, §28.8.1 (The field-restoration rule; Exception paths are not exempt), §28.11 (Indexer setter on a moved-from slot), §9.4, K3.11, K5.6, K9.2, K9.5, #5725
cells.note: Ordinary overwrite of an owned field (incl. through `set(owned)`, route below): once-backstopped, since the displaced value is disposed once after the RHS and a surviving field-held or element borrow meets the K4.1 flag (K5.6). Open: whether the 'not moved-from' half of the liveness test is the static per-slot fact or a run-time test. `move o.f` is admitted at any receiver (#5725 tracks the implementation), the moved-from state is tracked per receiver spelling, and §9.4 concedes it does not follow aliases of the holder. Reading A (static): when `o` aliases `this`, the restoring store `o._r := t` is compiled as a plain store and silently overwrites the value the aliased store put there, which is a leak with no backstop. Reading B (run time): a vacated owned field holds null and every owned-field store disposes a non-null displaced value, so nothing leaks, but then the restoring store is throwable under aliasing, contrary to §28.8.1's non-throwable inventory.

cells.rule: §28.11: "takes `owned`; indexer-set disposes the previous value first (skipped for a moved-from slot)" | §28.11: "The indexer-set disposes the displaced value per [§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields)'s drop-on-overwrite ([K3.11](#sec-kernel-k3)) — no explicit `Dispose()` at the assignment site" | §28.11: "An element-level write — an indexer-set — does not draw this warning" | §28.7: "a borrow of the displaced value is invalidated at the overwrite, caught as `DisposedAccessException` in checked disposal mode and undefined unchecked"
cells.cite: §28.11 (slot policy; Owning collections; move on a collection slot), §23.3 (`set(owned)`), §28.7, K3.11, K5.6, K4.1, stdlib §4.5, §4.9, §4.14
cells.note: The owning indexer-set (`set(owned)`) disposes the displaced element once, skipping a vacated slot; an element borrow of the displaced value is not frozen (K5.6) and meets the K4.1 flag the disposal sets (the indexer-set is a chosen silence of the use-after-removal warning, backstopped). A throwing displaced disposer raises inside the setter, whose `owned` `value` parameter is then discharged by the setter's exception-path discharge (§28.8.1), so the new value is not leaked. Because the setter is a member body, its moved-from skip can only be the slot's run-time null, so RC1's aliasing leak does not reach heap owning collections. §28.11's 'compiler's per-slot moved-from tracking' sentence reads as if it were static, though (RC1 note).

cells.rule: §15.3: "then each slot of the displaced value that is **live** — non-null and not moved-from, §28.7's liveness test — is disposed, **in reverse slot order**; then the new value is stored." | §35.4: "Whole-value reassignment of an owning-choice local or field *disposes the displaced value* per [§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields), like an owned class binding." | §35.9: "`null` assignment into an owned-state `C?` location is drop-on-overwrite" | K3.11: "reassignment of an owned location — a consume of the **displaced** value (drop-on-overwrite, [§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields))" | §28.7: "Scope: `owned` fields, plain-`var` owned locals, and — for whole-value reassignment — move-only value locals and instance fields; `using var` locals are not reassignable at all" | §9.4: "a read of the vacated field through an alias of its holder, which the moved-from state of [§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression) does not track, reads the same state."
cells.note: Decided sub-shapes: whole-value reassignment of an owning inline array (per live slot, reverse slot order, self-assignment a no-op, RHS-first) and of an owning choice or `C?` (single value; `:= null` drops). Local reassignment is frozen under live borrows (K5.2); a field reassignment is runtime-checked through §9.4's disposed state and per-object flags. Open: (1) a slot store `arr[i] := e` reaches the displaced-slot drop only through K3.11's 'owned location', since §28.7's scope sentence names whole-value reassignment only and §15.1.1's four endings omit slot stores (editorial, RC6). (2) At an inline-array field, a slot vacated by `move o._slots[i]` through an alias of the holder is RC1's ambiguity: a statically moved-from restoring store overwrites a live slot with no disposal.

cells.rule: §30.11: "The `Set*` methods complete the task; `TrySet*` returns `false` instead of throwing when the task is already in a terminal state." | §30.11: "If `TrySetResult` returns `false` because the task is already in a terminal state, the implementation disposes `result` before returning." | §28.8.1: "If the call then raises — from the callee's body, or from a constructor's field initializers or body ([§22.9](#sec-owned-fields-and-exception-safety)) — the caller's binding is moved-from on the exception edge exactly as on the normal one, and the value is discharged on the callee's side" | §31.2: "the superseded exception is **disposed by the runtime exactly once**, as if its handling had completed"
cells.note: Runtime-held slots are write-once: a task's result or fault is set at its terminal state and never displaced. A second `Set*` throws, and its `owned` argument is the stdlib method's parameter, discharged on the callee's side by §28.8.1; a failing `TrySet*` disposes its argument. The in-flight exception's 'displacement' is supersession, disposed once after its snapshot is recorded, with the two owner-owned instances dropped undisposed. Static task caches overwritten in place are R9's exemption.

cells.rule: §28.12: "The implicit disposal paths — auto-drop of a plain-`var` owned local or undischarged `owned` parameter at scope end, the exception-path cleanup, drop-on-overwrite, container cascades, and frame teardown" | §28.12: "always take the synchronous `Dispose()` path, on every edge and in every context including `async` bodies" | K5: "the frame's own disposal — explicit, at a `using var`'s scope end, or [K3.14](#sec-kernel-k3)'s auto-drop — counting as a use" | §29.7: "When a consumer stops iterating early — `break`, exception, or `using var` ending before exhaustion — the iterator is disposed."
cells.cite: §28.7, §28.12 (Implicit discharge is synchronous), §29.7, §29.8, §30.1, K5.5, K6.3, K3.11
cells.note: A frame-resident owned local or `owned` parameter reassigned in an iterator or `async` body takes §28.7 unchanged, synchronously, and it is never awaited. A local holding a frame (K6.3: calls mint) that is reassigned disposes the displaced frame, which runs its pending cleanup (§29.7), and the reassignment is frozen while borrows the old frame carries are live, since its disposal counts as a use (K5.5). Surviving non-local borrows meet the K4.1 flag. No escape found.

cells.rule: §22.12: "**Overwrite:** overwriting an admitted mutable static never disposes the displaced referent — deliberately *not* [§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields)'s drop-on-overwrite; the displaced referent remains alive until process exit" | §22.12: "slot stores, `move arr[j]`, and per-slot restoration follow [§15.1.1](#sec-owning-inline-arrays) unchanged" | §22.12: "whole-field reassignment is a **plain store that never auto-disposes displaced slots**" | §28.7: "**static** fields never take drop-on-overwrite for *any* type" | §22.8: "the field is also assigned **at most once**"
cells.cite: §22.8 (single assignment), §22.12 rule 2 (forms (i)–(iv), store semantics), §22.13 (exemption; static-overwrite posture), §28.7, §15.1.1, #5387, #5487
cells.note: `static owned readonly` (and form (h)): no displacement, single assignment (n/a in effect). Admitted non-`owned` mutable statics and form (iv)'s whole-field reassignment: exempt by the recorded no-drop posture (warned at form (iv)). Open: a **slot** store into a form-(iv) static. §22.12 sends slot stores to §15.1.1, which states no slot-store displacement at all, and §28.7 says statics never take drop-on-overwrite 'for any type'. Reading A: the displaced slot is dropped as at an instance field. Reading B: it is a plain store, so the displaced object leaves every enrolled slot and is never disposed (the exit pass disposes only current slots), and no warning names it. #5387/#5487 (static property stores) are borrow-side and do not decide this.

cells.rule: K1.6: "Values of runtime-managed type (`string`, `Type`, boxed value types, function values) and of ordinary value type carry no classification and no obligation" | §28.9: "Function-typed fields, parameters, and locals are not subject to `owned` annotations and carry no disposal obligation"
cells.note: Overwriting a `string`, `Type`, box or function value displaces no obligation. Hunted: a function-typed field whose closure captured an owned local (the capture is a borrow, rejected past its source, §28.9), and an interface-typed owned field holding a box (the drop is §28.9's no-op). Nothing obligation-bearing is displaced silently.

cells.rule: §28.3: "The implicit cleanup ordering follows reverse declaration order across multiple owned locals in the same scope, mirroring the destructor's field-disposal rule ([§28.4](#sec-the-destructor))." | §28.3: "Undischarged `owned` parameters' implicit disposals are established at entry to the body" | §29.8: "The order across multiple owned parameters is reverse declaration order, mirroring [§28.4](#sec-the-destructor)'s destructor rule." | §28.4: "a throwing disposer does not skip the remaining values: every remaining disposal still runs. If a later disposal in the same pass also throws, the later exception **supersedes** the earlier one"
cells.note: Several owned locals are disposed in reverse declaration order, inner scopes first, and a throwing disposer leaves the rest running with supersession: decided. Missing (order only): several undischarged `owned` parameters of a synchronous method, constructor or lambda are all 'established at entry to the body' with no order among them. §29.8 and §30.1 state reverse declaration order for iterator and async frames, and nothing states it for the synchronous body. Exactly-once holds either way; the observable destructor order does not.

cells.rule: §28.10: "pending cleanups run in reverse order of establishment" | §28.10: "ordered against neighbouring cleanups exactly as a hand-written `using var` at the same line would be." | §28.4: "a throwing disposer does not skip the remaining values: every remaining disposal still runs. If a later disposal in the same pass also throws, the later exception **supersedes** the earlier one"
cells.note: Named, anonymous and compiler-introduced scope pins share one establishment-ordered stack with `finally` on every edge, so a `for` loop's `__enumerator` is disposed before its `__source`. Scope-end disposal of several locals is a named multi-value pass, in which a throwing disposer does not stop the rest and later throws supersede with record-before-drop. A borrow-pin contributes nothing to the pass. No escape found.

cells.rule: K8: "Unbound owned temporaries are disposed at their full expression's end, after their uses; on the exception edge, during unwinding in reverse production order." | K3.15: "**Edge parity.** The exception edge performs the same implicit disposal as the normal edge, on the single establishment-ordered cleanup stack; the only difference is the lint. Unbound temporaries join the same stack at their production." | K8: "disposed at the atom's completion if undischarged, after the body's evaluation, in reverse clause order" | §28.4: "the exception-path discharge (including the unwind disposal of an expression's produced temporaries, [§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries))"
cells.cite: K8.1, K8.3, K8.5, K3.15, §28.3 (Unbound owned temporaries), §28.4, §28.10
cells.note: Temporaries join the cleanup stack at production, so they leave it in reverse production order on both edges (K3.15). K8.1 spells out the order for the exception edge only, and the normal-edge order follows from the shared stack. Binding-atom bindings go in reverse clause order, and a `case` scrutinee's temporary lasts the whole construct. Throwing temporaries' disposers take the multi-value discipline. No escape found.

cells.rule: §28.4: "Runs the destructor body, if any." | §28.4: "Destructors run in subclass-to-base order." | §28.4: "Before it propagates, the **remaining steps of the generated `Dispose()` still run**" | §22.10: "the reverse-declaration-order disposal pass therefore disposes captures *before* declared fields" | §28.4: "a throwing disposer does not skip the remaining values: every remaining disposal still runs. If a later disposal in the same pass also throws, the later exception **supersedes** the earlier one"
cells.note: A generated `Dispose()` runs the destructor body, then the owned fields in reverse declaration order (captures first), then the base chain. A throw anywhere keeps the remaining steps running, with later throws superseding under record-before-drop. A destructor's `move` of a field skips that field in the pass, and the destructor must discharge the taken value. Re-entrant use of the object from a child's destructor during the field pass meets the K4.1 flag. The ownership-cycle escape is filed as a route cell below.

cells.rule: §28.11: "**reverse storage order** for the ordered collections — descending index for `OwningArray`, tail-to-head for `OwningLinkedList`, pop order for `OwningStack`, the reverse of dequeue order for `OwningQueue`, descending slot index for `OwningSlotMap`" | §28.11: "implementation-defined for the unordered (`OwningDictionary`, `OwningSet`). `Clear()` disposes the elements it holds in that same order and keeps the emptied collection." | §28.4: "an owning collection's element cascade" | §28.4: "a throwing disposer does not skip the remaining values: every remaining disposal still runs. If a later disposal in the same pass also throws, the later exception **supersedes** the earlier one"
cells.note: The cascade order is stated per type (unordered types are explicitly implementation-defined), and the cascade is a named multi-value pass: a throwing element disposer does not stop the rest. `Clear()` and `Remove*` are not named as multi-value passes, and whether the slots are emptied when a disposer throws mid-`Clear()` is not stated. Under every reading an element left in place has already been flagged, so the later cascade's second Dispose is §28.2's no-op and an indexer read through it faults under K4.1. Exactly-once holds, though it rests on idempotence (worth a note, not an issue). #4777 (`OwningSlotMap<T>`) is implementation-only.

cells.rule: §15.1.1: "When an owning inline array's lifetime ends, the array's auto-dispose pass disposes each non-null slot, **in reverse slot order**" | §35.4: "Disposing an owning choice value disposes the active case's `owned` payloads (in payload declaration order) and, recursively, any move-only payloads" | §28.4: "Disposes all owned-bearing fields in reverse declaration order. This covers fields marked `owned` (class- or interface-typed; the field's value's `Dispose()` is called) and fields of owning-inline-array type" | §28.4: "Inline-array fields without `owned` slots, value-typed fields, and runtime-managed fields require no disposal." | §35.4: "a move-only value carrying no borrows may be a class field (the class's destructor disposes it)" | §28.9: "it has no destructor, no `owned` fields of non-trivial-dispose type, no fields of owning-inline-array type"
cells.note: Owning inline arrays: reverse slot order, a multi-value pass, the holder's destruction leaving §9.4's disposed state: once. Owning-choice values held in locals or temporaries: active-case payloads in **forward** declaration order (the one forward-ordered pass in the chapter, though it is stated). Conflict at an instance field: §15.3/§35.4 say the class's destructor disposes an owning-choice field, but §28.4 step 2's owned-bearing enumeration omits it and files value-typed fields under 'require no disposal'. §28.9's trivial-dispose definition likewise omits it, so a class whose only obligation is an owning-choice field is trivial-dispose by the letter, and its free 'runs no user code'. #5642/#5541 track the disposed state, not this enumeration.

cells.rule: §28.4: "a pass entered with **no exception in flight** whose N disposers all throw leaves the escaping exception carrying N−1 chronological entries" | §31.2: "a superseded task-owned fault instance ([§30.9](#sec-exception-handling-in-async-methods)) or cached `TypeInitializationException` ([§31.4](#sec-standard-exception-types)) is dropped from the in-flight slot **undisposed**" | §31.2: "**Self-supersession records nothing:**"
cells.note: Ordinary in-flight and superseded exceptions in a pass: each superseded one is snapshotted into the superseder's `SupersededChain` and then disposed once (once). Task-owned faults and the cached TIE are dropped undisposed and stay with their owner (exempt). Accounting: N−1 entries with no exception in flight, plus the in-flight exception's own entry ahead of them on an exception edge. The exit pass reports rather than propagates. No escape.

cells.rule: §29.7: "in reverse order of establishment, exactly as if the body had exited at the suspension point" | §29.8: "If the body does not move ownership out, the state machine disposes the parameter at iterator disposal — after `using var` cleanups within the body and after `finally` clauses. The order across multiple owned parameters is reverse declaration order" | §30.1: "on every completion path (success, fault, and cancellation), after the body's `using var` cleanups and `finally` clauses, in reverse declaration order"
cells.note: Frame teardown runs the pending `using var`/`finally` cleanups in reverse establishment as an exit at the suspension point, then the undischarged `owned` parameters in reverse declaration order, on every terminal path. A throwing cleanup turns the teardown into an exception edge on which the remaining cleanups and parameter disposals still run (K3.15), with §28.4 supersession. No escape on order or exactly-once (the re-iterable owned-parameter case is the pilot's R8/C11, not this column).

cells.rule: §22.13: "Static `owned` fields are disposed at program exit, after `Main` completes (normally, or by an uncaught exception — [§33.3](#sec-exit-code) defines the exit code for each), in **reverse order of static initialization** across all types" | §22.13: "**What escapes the pass is reported, not propagated.**" | §22.13: "Static `owned` fields initialized during the pass join it" | §22.13: "The field is not disposed at program exit and must not hold resources that require explicit cleanup."
cells.cite: §22.12 rule 1, §22.13 (Disposal of static owned fields; throwing destructor; exemption; abnormal termination), §15.1.1, §28.4, §31.2, §33.3
cells.note: `static owned` and owning-inline-array statics: the exit pass disposes them once, in reverse initialization order across types and reverse declaration order within a type (slots in reverse), draining late initializations. Throws are superseded with N−1 entries and reported to stderr, and the exit code is unchanged: once. Non-`owned` statics: exempt. Abnormal termination is a recorded non-guarantee. Re-population of an already-disposed static during the pass is a route cell below.

cells.rule: §15.1.1: "A slot of interface type holding a boxed value type ([§8.6](#sec-boxing)) holds a runtime-managed value ([§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types)): the pass runs no user code for it, the box's `Dispose()` being §28.9's no-op." | K1.6: "Values of runtime-managed type (`string`, `Type`, boxed value types, function values) and of ordinary value type carry no classification and no obligation"
cells.note: A runtime-managed value inside a pass (a boxed slot, a string or function field) contributes a no-op step and no supersession. Hunted: a closure held in a field of an object in a pass that captured an owned referent (capture is a borrow; reclaiming the closure never leaves a destructor un-run, §28.9). Nothing obligation-bearing rides the exemption.

cells.rule: K3.3: "an `owned` argument ([§22.3](#sec-parameter-modifiers)) | `move x` at the call site | **moved-from** | frozen (K5.1) | none here — the callee's" | §28.8.1: "The transfer of an `owned` argument completes when the call is **entered**" | K3.13: "An **unmarked read of a class-typed binding never consumes**" | K5: "Consuming an owned **binding** (a local or `owned` parameter; the consume table's positions) while a live local borrow of its current value exists is a compile error" | §28.3: "A borrow is *live* at a consume site when some path from the site reaches a later use of it — [K5.5](#sec-kernel-k5)'s body-local backward dataflow, traced directly, through a `using var` pin ([§28.10](#sec-using-var)), or through a closure value that is itself still live." | §28.3: "Parameter `p` (no modifier) | Borrowed (source: caller)" | K4.3: "no new admission may be made without recording its clause or its backstop"
cells.cite: K3 table (K3.1–K3.4, K3.7), K3.13, K5, K5.5, K4.3, §22.3, §22.4, §22.5, §28.3 (Move semantics; consume-site freeze; Producers), §28.8.1 (raise from the consuming call), App. C.3; #5565, #5523, #5551
cells.note: Every marked transfer of an owned local or `owned` parameter of a synchronous body leaves it moved-from, the new holder discharges, the scope-end and unwind passes skip it, and a raise after entry stays with the callee (§28.8.1); an unmarked read only borrows; a later read is an error; `out owned` delivers only on normal return. Hunted and closed: `M(move x, x.F())` (second operand reads a moved-from binding), a later-argument throw before entry (caller's unwind), a `catch` re-dispose (binding unreadable). Open: a plain argument that borrows `x` in the same call that takes `move x` (`Sink(x, move x)`, `Sink(x.Child(), move x)`). Reading 1: the call's use of the earlier-evaluated argument is a later use of a live borrow, so the move is frozen and rejected. Reading 2: the freeze's subject is a *local* borrow (K5's wording; K5.5 enumerates locals, pins and closures), the argument is a temporary, and the call is admitted; the callee then holds a plain parameter, which it reads as caller-sourced and valid for the call, aliasing its own `owned` parameter, and can move that parameter to another domain (no flag is ever set, K4.3) and keep reading the alias, with no recorded clause.

cells.rule: K7.4: "owned ⊓ moved-from and owned ⊓ explicitly-disposed = **maybe-consumed** — unreadable after the join, no flow around a back edge into a use; scope-end disposal per-path" | §28.3: "join to **maybe-consumed** the variable may not be read, borrowed from, or consumed, and may not flow around a loop back edge into any use, while scope-end auto-drop applies per-path" | K1: "**moved-from** — the obligation has transferred out; the binding or slot is unreadable until reassigned, and discharge machinery skips it" | K3.11: "reassignment of an owned location — a consume of the **displaced** value" | §28.3: "Two states qualify, and no others" | §28.7: "if the previous value is live (non-null and not moved-from — the per-slot tracking [§28.11](#sec-collection-element-ownership)'s indexer-set rule already defines), it is disposed" | K7.3: "owned ⊓ borrowed = **rejected**"
cells.cite: K1 (states 3–4), K3.11, K7, §28.3 (Ownership state of locals; State match; Adoption; Producers `??`/if rows), §28.7, §20, §19.2, §22.4 (`out using var` per path); #3967 (impl, under reading 1)
cells.note: Decided: owned ⊓ owned carries one obligation (exactly one arm's value exists); owned ⊓ borrowed is rejected; a conditional kill of any consume-table row joins to maybe-consumed, unreadable, with per-path scope-end auto-drop; an uninitialized or polymorphic-null local adopts per path; a marked arm `move x` consumes only on its selected path; null and throw arms absorb; an `out using var` obligation attaches only on paths where the call returned. Hunted and closed: a mixed meet (K7.3), an all-borrow arm-meet at `using var` (R2). Open: reassignment of a maybe-consumed local, and the admissible RHS at a definitely moved-from one. K1 says moved-from is unreadable 'until reassigned' and §28.7's liveness test is per-path, so reading 1 admits `x := new R();` and drops the displaced value only on the still-owned path. But K3.11 makes reassignment 'a consume of the displaced value', §28.3 says a maybe-consumed binding 'may not be ... consumed', and the state-match/adoption paragraphs cover owned-state, borrowed-state, uninitialized and polymorphic-null LHSs only ('Two states qualify, and no others'), so reading 2 rejects the store and leaves no rule for the RHS's classification. The implementation follows reading 1 and drops the moved pointer on the taken path (#3967, heap-use-after-free). The text names neither the reading nor the per-path drop.

cells.rule: K7.4: "owned ⊓ moved-from and owned ⊓ explicitly-disposed = **maybe-consumed** — unreadable after the join, no flow around a back edge into a use; scope-end disposal per-path" | §28.3: "join to **maybe-consumed** the variable may not be read, borrowed from, or consumed, and may not flow around a loop back edge into any use, while scope-end auto-drop applies per-path" | K3.14: "An owned value that reaches its scope's end undischarged and not moved-from is disposed there implicitly" | §29.2: "the "fall-through to the next iteration" edge is checked the same way as the body's end" | K3.11: "reassignment of an owned location — a consume of the **displaced** value" | K1: "**moved-from** — the obligation has transferred out; the binding or slot is unreadable until reassigned, and discharge machinery skips it"
cells.cite: K3.14, K7 (back edges), K7.4, K8.2, §21.4, §21.5, §28.3 (Move semantics: loop accumulator; Ownership state of locals), §29.2, §28.14 v1 bound 2(a)
